# Attributes

Attributes written `@(name)` or `@(name=value)`. The ones marked Vidar control `-opt` and the checks; see [Faster code](../language/optimization.md).

- `cold`: Hints that the procedure is rarely called.
- `deprecated`: Warns on use, with a message.
- `disabled`: Removes calls to the procedure when the condition is true.
- `export`: Exports the symbol from the binary.
- `fini`: Runs the procedure after `main` returns.
- `hot`: Vidar: with `-opt`, every decision against something inside this procedure is a warning: a bounds check left in, an indirect call, an allocation in a loop, a closure not inlined.
- `init`: Runs the procedure before `main`.
- `link_name`: The symbol name used for linking.
- `memo`: Vidar: each outer call gets a memo table that the procedure's calls to itself share, freed when it returns: an array when every parameter is bool, u8 or i8 (4096 results at most), else a map. `-opt` adds it on its own to pure integer procedures that call themselves more than once per call.
- `no_alloc`: Vidar: a compile error when this procedure, or anything it calls, can allocate: `make`, `new`, `append`, map inserts, allocating `core:` procs, or a call through a closure or interface whose targets aren't all known. Builds below `-o:size` also give it a panicking allocator.
- `no_memo`: Vidar: `-opt` won't memoize this procedure on its own.
- `no_perfect_hash`: Vidar: `-opt` won't turn this procedure's string switches (8 or more literal cases) into a perfect-hash lookup.
- `no_specialize`: Vidar: `-opt` won't make specialized copies of this procedure on its own.
- `no_stack_buffer`: Vidar: `-opt` won't put this procedure's constant-size `make`s (freed by a `defer delete`) on the stack.
- `no_table`: Vidar: `-opt` won't turn this procedure into a lookup table on its own.
- `private`: Hides a declaration from other packages (`@(private="file")`: from other files).
- `require_results`: Warns when a call's results are ignored.
- `specialize`: Vidar: calls passing constants to basic or enum parameters call a copy where those parameters are compile-time (`$p`).
- `static`: Makes a local variable live for the whole program.
- `table`: Vidar: stores the result for every value of the one `bool`, `u8`, `i8` or enum parameter (or every pair of values of two `bool`, `u8` or `i8` parameters), and turns calls into a table lookup. The body must depend only on its arguments.
- `thread_local`: Gives each thread its own copy of a global.
